tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Who SigmaJunction is: practices, engagement models, how engagements start, markets, languages and contact details.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: SigmaJunction's three practices and their capabilities, with links to each service page.

tools.name: get_engagement_models
tools.description: How working with SigmaJunction is priced: dedicated team, per project with milestone billing, or an equity partnership; plus the cost guide and the free diagnosis.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Any page of sigmajunction.com as Markdown, by path ("/pricing", "/de/work") or by full URL on sigmajunction.com.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: SigmaJunction's articles (title, summary, date, link), newest first, optionally filtered by a search term.

tools.name: send_inquiry
tools.description: Send a project inquiry to SigmaJunction on the user's behalf. Only use when the user has asked to contact SigmaJunction, and confirm the name, email and message with them first. A partner replies by email within one business day.

tools.name: request_partner_checklist
tools.description: Email the user SigmaJunction's two-page checklist for choosing a software development partner (PDF). Only use when the user asked for it and gave their email address. Newsletter sign-up only if the user explicitly wants it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_page · Private data: get_company_profile, send_inquiry · Public sink: send_inquiry, request_partner_checklist.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_page · Private data: get_company_profile, send_inquiry · Public sink: send_inquiry, request_partner_checklist

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
